title: Silas and the Inheritance
premise: Edmund Galloway, a night-shift dispatcher who has spent fifteen years erasing himself from the town of Marlow Bend, finds a drowned man wearing Edmund's own missing coat—and in the pocket, a note naming a witness who supposedly died years ago. As Edmund investigates, he discovers the dead man was hired to find that witness: a woman Edmund helped disappear after she saw something terrible, a secret Edmund has been paid to keep buried ever since. The inheritance in question is not money but testimony, and the killer is the town patriarch whose family fortune depends on the witness staying dead. Edmund must choose between the invisibility that kept him safe and the truth that could destroy him, and in the end he brings the witness home to testify, sacrificing his own anonymity—and learning that survival purchased with silence was never really survival at all.
about_author: Lena Montrose is the pen name of a former small-town court stenographer who spent a decade listening to what people swore they'd never say aloud. She writes mysteries about the quiet people who keep towns running and secrets buried.

chapters.title: The Night Shift
chapters.summary: Edmund Galloway's POV. We meet Edmund mid-shift, a man who has made himself a filing system for other people's secrets: fares, affairs, alibis. A call comes in about a body at the reservoir, and the responding driver mentions the dead man was wearing a distinctive wool coat. Edmund's stomach drops—it's his, missing from his closet a week ago. Emotional beat: dread cracking open a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: Clothes That Don't Fit
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. At the reservoir, Sheriff Dane Voss questions Edmund, who lies smoothly about the coat. Searching the corpse's pockets, Edmund finds a torn note: 'The witness in the Hollis case is alive. Ask the dispatcher.' The Hollis case—a woman named Ruth Hollis who vanished in 2009, presumed drowned. Edmund recognizes the handwriting of a missing persons investigator. Emotional beat: the past reaching through fifteen years of silence.

chapters.title: Alphabetized Ghosts
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, with flashbacks. Edmund digs into his own meticulous logs and finds the calls he once routed to a safehouse the night Ruth Hollis disappeared—calls he was paid, in cash, by an intermediary, to lose. He remembers Ruth's face through a taxi window. The investigator's last logged call came from the Ashcombe estate. Emotional beat: guilt surfacing like a body in water.

chapters.title: The Ashcombe Fortune
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. He researches the Hollis case at the library: Ruth witnessed a hit-and-run that killed a young mechanic—a crime tied to Charles Ashcombe's son, whose death would have voided the family's controlling trust. The 'witness' is the only living proof. Edmund realizes someone is hunting Ruth before the trust's final settlement clause triggers this winter. Emotional beat: understanding the price of survival—hers and his.

chapters.title: A Fare to Nowhere
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: Edmund and a mysterious woman calling herself 'Vera' who books a cab to a crossroads outside town. Edmund recognizes the address from his old logs—Ruth's old escape route. He drives her himself and, in the mirror, sees Ruth Hollis alive, older, watchful. She tells him to forget her again. Emotional beat: the impossible made flesh; old loyalty versus old fear.

chapters.title: What the Sheriff Knows
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Sheriff Voss confronts Edmund with the coat evidence and offers a deal: help him find Ruth and Edmund stays out of prison. But Edmund notices Voss's case files are thin in exactly the places Ashcombe money touches—the sheriff is compromised. Edmund realizes the law itself is part of the trap. Emotional beat: isolation; nowhere safe to turn.

chapters.title: The Intermediary
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Edmund tracks the man who once paid him: a retired lawyer named Pell, now dying, who confesses he was Ashcombe's fixer and that the dead investigator was his own hire—a man who grew a conscience. Pell gives Edmund a key to a safety deposit box holding Ruth's original signed statement. That night, Pell's house burns. Emotional beat: the cost of truth made literal; ticking clock.

chapters.title: Dead Drop
chapters.summary: Edmund and Ruth's POV alternate. Edmund retrieves the statement while Voss and Ashcombe's men close in; a chase through the rail yard ends with Edmund wounded but escaping. Ruth, hiding in a decommissioned motel, decides she's done running—she saw what silence cost Pell and the investigator. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into resolve; two fugitives from the same night finally on the same side.

chapters.title: The Settlement
chapters.summary: Climax. Edmund's POV. At the Ashcombe estate, where the family gathers to sign the trust's final settlement, Edmund walks in—visible for the first time in fifteen years—and plays the recording of Pell's confession while Ruth arrives with the signed statement and a state investigator Edmund secretly alerted. Charles Ashcombe orders his men to take them; Voss, forced to choose, arrests the Ashcombes instead. Emotional beat: the invisible man made unmistakably seen.

chapters.title: Day Shift
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV, weeks later. Ruth testifies; the trust dissolves into restitution for the mechanic's family. Edmund quits the night shift and takes a day job driving the school route—out in the daylight, known by name. He visits Ruth, and they share coffee like two people who survived the same war. Final line lands the theme: some inheritances you spend, and some you carry. Emotional beat: quiet, earned peace.
